newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro foreign minister killed in car crash.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro foreign minister killed in car crash.

text.p: Janko Jeknic, foreign minister of the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro, was killed on Friday when his car crashed into a bus, an official statement said.
Jeknic's car ran into a bus that was stopped by the side of the Podgorica-Danilovgrad road at Novo Selo at 6:30 a.m. (0530 GMT), the information ministry said in a statement.
It said that the roads were icy at the time and that no one on board the bus was injured.

The Montenegrin news agency Montena-fax said a woman passenger in the car was seriously injured while the Beta news agency reported that a passenger in the car had died. The information ministry would not comment on the reports.
The ministry said a funeral would be held in Podgorica on Saturday.

Tanjug, the Yugoslav news agency, said Jeknic, 47, had a university degree in economics and served as head of protocol and consul for economic affairs in the Yugoslav consulate in Milan, Italy, before becoming foreign minister.

Montenegro, a small, mountainous territory flanking the Adriatic Sea, and the larger, more populous Serbia are the only republics left in federal Yugoslavia after the secession of four others in 1991-92.
The moderate Montenegrin leadership has been critical of leftist Serbia's resistance to democratic reform and privatisation, fearing this will prolong Yugoslavia's international isolation.
